ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Republic of Korea governs AML/CFT through the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6776, as amended), the Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secrecy Act (Act No. 5493, as amended), the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 6516, as amended), the Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended). The Korean Financial Intelligence Unit, operating under the Financial Services Commission, supervises financial institutions and designated non-financial businesses and professions, which must perform customer due diligence and report suspicious transactions under the statutory AML framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate corporate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The competent company registry in the country of origin (e.g., State of Delaware, Division of Corporations) or the Supreme Court of Korea if the parent is Korean
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: notarize the certified copy if required by the origin authority, then obtain an Apostille from the competent Hague Apostille authority of the origin state because the Republic of Korea is a Party to the Hague Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization route, which applies only when the origin state is not an Apostille Convention member: verify the document at the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Korean Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction over the origin state. The two routes are mutually exclusive; never apply both in sequence. Submit the apostilled or legalized original together with a certified Korean translation and translator's affidavit to the Korean registration office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (recent official status certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or tax authority in the country of origin of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: obtain an official certificate from the registry, notarize if required, and affix an Apostille issued by the relevant Hague Authority. Consular Legalization route, for non-Apostille states only: obtain verification from the origin state foreign affairs ministry, then legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Do not chain the apostille with consular legalization. The Korean adoption bank will additionally require a certified Korean translation and proof of current registration for the customer due diligence file.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the sole shareholder and Power of Attorney authorizing local incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The board of directors of the ultimate parent entity and a notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin state is an Apostille Convention member, sign the resolution before a notary where necessary and obtain an Apostille from the notary's competent authority. If the origin state is not a member, proceed only with consular legalization after notarization and foreign ministry attestation. The apostille and consular legalization methods are alternatives, never sequential. The resolution must explicitly approve the formation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, the registered office, the UBO disclosure to KoFIU and financial institutions, and the delegates' authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (constitutive charter) of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The incorporators and a Korean notary public who certifies the articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For internal Korean documents, the articles are notarized under the Notary Fee Act. Foreign shareholder execution pages, if notarized outside Korea, must follow either the Apostille route for Hague member states or the Consular Legalization route for non-member states. The two routes are parallel and exclusive; do not combine them. The Korean notarial certificate is the operative authentication for the Korean registry file, while any foreign public document is authenticated under the Hague Convention or Korean consular law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a financial institution maintaining the shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The account-holding bank in the country of origin, signed by a branch manager or compliance officer under a FATF-compliant AML jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be issued on bank letterhead and as a signed original. If the origin state is an Apostille Convention member, the bank signature may be apostilled after a notary certifies the signature. If the origin state is not a member, the notarized signature must be verified by the origin foreign ministry and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives; never use both in the same chain. The Korean bank will require the original and a certified Korean translation before account opening.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and before opening any Korean bank account, the ultimate shareholder, every individual UBO holding at least 25%, all directors, officers, and authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Korean KoFIU high-risk trade and cash payment guidance, and the domestic blacklist of persons subject to financial sanctions under the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Each screened person is also checked for Korean domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, including immediate family and close associates, with a risk-rating matrix adopted from the FATF and Wolfsberg principles. Domestic PEPs require senior management approval; foreign PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions require enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds evidence, and weekly re-screening until account opening is completed.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IRO (Internet Registration Office) of the Supreme Court of Korea (www.iros.go.kr), operated by the Court Administration Office, using the corporate registration search and name-reservation module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name of a Korean entity must be expressed in the Hangul script under Commercial Act registration practice; the registry does not accept a foreign-language-only name as the main trade name. English names may be used only as a transliterated sub-name, shown in parentheses or disclosed in the English portion of the registration certificate, but the Korean recognition and seizure of the name depends on the Hangul name. The Korean name must follow a four-tier conventional structure: a distinctive core word, an optional business-objective word describing the subscription-box commerce, an optional permissible geographic or emblematic marker, and the entity-type suffix Yuhan Hoesa or, if a stock company is selected, Chusik Hoesa. The name must be distinguishable from all previously registered trade names in Korea under the same type of business, and must not be identical to a name whose registration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, particularly Articles 37, 543 through 613 governing a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), and the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court or the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, under the Supreme Court Registry Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa under Articles 543 through 613 of the Commercial Act. However, the full amount of each member's subscribed contribution must be actually paid in cash or in kind by the time of incorporation, and the cash contribution must be deposited into a designated bank escrow or temporary capital payment account in Korea before registration. The bank-issued certificate of contribution payment must be submitted to the registry court. There is no fixed statutory blocking period, but the deposited funds remain restricted until the incorporation certificate is issued. Where the business seeks certain tax incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investment of KRW 100,000,000 or more may be required for those incentives, but that is not a corporate incorporation capital requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE SUBSCRIBER-MEMBERS ACTING AS THE ORGAN OF YUHANGHOESA (a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea) AT THE FIRST GENERAL MEETING OF MEMBERS, AND RATIFIED BY THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS AT THE INAUGURAL MEETING OF DIRECTORS, HELD ON [DATE] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE. WHEREAS the subscribers have prepared and notarized Articles of Incorporation for the formation of a limited liability company under the Commercial Act; and WHEREAS the total capital of KRW 10,000,000 has been allocated by subscription amounts stated in the subscription register; NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The certified Articles of Incorporation are adopted in their entirety as the supreme governance instrument of the Company. 2. The subscribed members and capital allocations set out in the subscription register are ratified, and each member shall pay the full amount of contribution in Korean Won to the temporary capital payment account designated by the board, with the bank certificate of contribution payment delivered to the registration agent. 3. The registered office of the Company shall be at the address stated in the Articles, being the principal place of business in the Republic of Korea, and the Company shall maintain the registered office through a lawful lease or title document. 4. [NAME] and [NAME] are appointed as the first directors of the Company. 5. [NAME] is appointed as representative director with sole authority to represent the Company in all corporate acts, to sign commercial instruments, to register the incorporation at the District Court, and to act as the statutory representative before any court or administrative agency. 6. The representative director and any other director designated by the board are jointly authorized to open and operate bank accounts in the name of the Company, to subscribe to online payment platforms including Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net, and to set authorized signatories, transaction limits, and recurring billing mandates. 7. The representative director is directed and empowered to file the incorporation registration application, pay all stamp duties and registration fees, obtain the corporate registration certificate, make the business registration with the National Tax Service, and file the online mail-order business report required for subscription box commerce. 8. The representative director shall secure all fire safety, building occupancy, environmental registration, and occupational safety approvals needed before warehouse fulfillment operations begin. 9. This resolution shall take immediate effect upon signature and seal by the organizing members and directors. Adopted unanimously on [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Article drafting, name search, and notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Commercial Register name-search portal and a Korean Notary Public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a priority name search using the Supreme Court commercial register name system to confirm that the proposed legal name does not conflict with an existing registered trade name. Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, stating the company type as a Yuhan Hoesa, the total capital, the exact purpose of recurring physical subscription box merchandising and fulfillment, the registered office address, and the duration. The Articles must be signed or sealed by every subscriber-member and notarized by a notary public. Any foreign corporate resolution or power of attorney must be apostilled or consular-legalized and accompanied by a notarized Korean translation before the notary accepts the document set.
required_dossiers: Passport or foreign corporate extract of each member
Hong Kong-style certificate of incumbency if shareholder is an entity
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Commitment letter to subscribe to membership interests
Notarized power of attorney for local formation agent
Name search confirmation receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is rejected, file an amended name list within one business day and pay no additional state fee beyond the new notary certificate. If the notary requests additional authentication, cure by obtaining an apostille or legalized Korean translation within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital contribution and bank certificate of payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Korea operating a foreign exchange and capital escrow desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital payment deposit account in the name of the promoter or a licensed local attorney escrow account at a Korean commercial bank. Remit the full subscribed capital in Korean Won from the foreign shareholder or an in-country investor, and instruct the bank to issue a Certificate of Contribution Deposit written in Korean, stating the deposited amount, account number, date, and beneficiary name. The certificate must exactly match the capital amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation. No withdrawal or transfer is permitted until the incorporation registration is completed and the temporary account is converted into or transferred to the corporate bank account.
required_dossiers: Promoter identification or passport
Remittance instruction and foreign exchange receipt
Articles of Incorporation excerpt showing capital
Capital payment schedule signed by members
Bank account opening application for temporary deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate amount or remitter name is queried, obtain a confirmatory letter from the bank and resubmit within one business day. If the remittance is held by foreign exchange control, provide the required source-of-funds statement and remit again without additional penalty if cured before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation registration at the District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the competent District Court in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation registration application to the court registry within two weeks after completion of capital payment, as required for a limited liability company. The representative director or authorized attorney must appear in person or file electronically through the court registration system. The filing must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank certificate of contribution payment, notices of appointment of directors and representative director, written consents of each director to accept office, copies of identification, and the certified power of attorney. The registry will verify the capital payment, corporate name, and governing provisions, then issue the Certificate of Corporate Registration and assign the business registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of contribution payment issued by bank
Appointment notification for directors and representative director
Consent and acceptance forms signed by each director
Power of attorney for registration agent
Identification of each subscriber-member and director
Proof of registered office lease or ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a supplementary order, cure the stated defect within seven days, pay the applicable correction fee if any, and resubmit through the electronic system. If the court rejects the application on substantive grounds, amend the Articles with a notary and file anew without sacrificing seniority if the resubmission occurs before the two-week deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service business registration and online mail-order report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service and the local municipal government responsible for communication sales business reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after issuance of the corporate registration certificate, file the business registration application with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office. Attach the certificate of corporate registration, lease agreement, proof of office address, and director identification. Because the subscription box service is a communication sales business under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce and Similar Transactions, the company must also file an online mail-order business report with the local municipal government, identifying the website, order-taking means, delivery methods, consumer service contact, and physical fulfillment center address. Both registrations may be completed through the Government24 digital portal.
required_dossiers: Certificate of corporate registration
Business registration application form
Lease or ownership document for registered office
Director identification and card copy
Website or online selling platform information
Online mail-order business report form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the application due to missing lease documents, present the landlord lease and building registration certificate within three business days. If the municipal mail-order report is queried because the fulfillment address differs, add a warehouse lease certificate and resubmit; no operation may commence until both certificates are issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical fulfillment, fire safety, and banking activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local fire station and National Fire Agency, local building administration, Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency, and the designated corporate bank branch.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing warehouse packaging and box assembly, obtain the fire safety completion certificate from the local fire station after inspection of automatic fire detection and suppression systems, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes. Obtain the building occupancy certificate and, if racking or shelving is installed, submit a structural engineer load certification to the local building administration. Register the workplace with the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, and appoint a safety and health manager if the workforce requires one. Finally, open the corporate current bank account using the incorporation certificate, and activate Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net after the bank account is active.
required_dossiers: Warehouse lease and building floor plan
Fire protection design and equipment specification
Fire safety inspection application submitted to local fire station
Structural load calculation for high-bay racking
Occupational safety and health registration form
Certificate of corporate registration
Bank account opening application
Payment processor onboarding and KYC documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire safety inspection fails, correct the defects within 30 days and request re-inspection. If the structural load certificate is rejected, obtain an amended engineer report and resubmit. If workplace safety registration is delayed, temporary suspension of warehouse operations is required until the Ministry of Employment and Labor issues acknowledgement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of SMEs and Startups; National Fire Agency; local municipal fire and building safety bureau; Ministry of Employment and Labor.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Online Mail-Order Business Report Certificate, Business Registration Certificate, Fire Safety Completion Certificate, and Workplace Establishment Notification.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is the applicable tier for a subscription-box fulfillment warehouse that does not involve hazardous chemical manufacturing, large-scale logistics complex construction, or a project site exceeding the full EIA screening threshold. A full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required only if the operation constructs a logistics complex, industrial estate, or cold-chain facility above the statutory size threshold, or stores hazardous substances requiring approval under the Chemicals Control Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge is expected from dry-goods subscription box assembly and dry warehousing. If any incidental wastewater is introduced into the public sewer, it must meet Sewerage Act parameters including pH 5.8 to 8.6, BOD below 300 mg/L, COD below 400 mg/L, and suspended solids below 300 mg/L as set by the local municipal sewer ordinance. Packaging adhesive solvent use must comply with Clean Air Conservation Act volatile organic compound emission limits, and facilities using solvent-based adhesives are required to maintain an emission inventory if annual VOC use exceeds one tonne. Hazardous waste, if any, must be stored separately, labeled, and removed by a licensed hazardous waste transporter under the Waste Management Act, with manifests submitted through the Allbaro waste tracking system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Fire Services Act is mandatory for the warehouse as a specific object and includes automatic fire detection, fire extinguishing equipment, emergency lighting, and evacuation route inspection by the local fire station. Civil defense self-inspection logs must be kept monthly and produced upon inspection. A building occupancy permit and structural load inspection are required before installing racking and shelving systems, and the certificate must be displayed at the facility. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the workplace must be registered with the Ministry of Employment and Labor, a safety and health management system established, and a safety and health manager appointed where the statutory threshold of employees is reached.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, Ministry of Economy and Finance; online portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (KCS) maintains the UNI-PASS clearance portal (https://unipass.customs.go.kr) for export declarations and customs audit evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine registration category. A Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation and must obtain a Business Registration Number (BRN) from the National Tax Service; the registration application is due within 20 days after business commencement and may be filed earlier. A foreign non-resident company without a Korean place of business must first appoint a resident tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes and file the appointment/power of attorney with the NTS. Step 2: Assemble statutory documents: Korean registry corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, shareholder register, board resolution appointing the Korean tax representative or domestic director, lease agreement or proof of place of business, and identity documents of the appointed representative. Step 3: Submit the business registration application through HomeTax or to the district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered Korean address. Step 4: After NTS validation, the entity receives a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the corporate TIN, VAT registration number, and e-tax invoice identification number; Korean law does not issue a separate VAT certificate. Step 5: Activate the HomeTax electronic filing profile, e-tax invoice transmission profile, and cash receipt system if B2C cash sales occur. Step 6: If the taxpayer is instead a non-resident foreign seller of physical merchandise to Korean consumers without any Korean establishment, the simplified foreign seller registration module in HomeTax may apply; for KR_YUHANGHOESA, the standard domestic corporate registration route is mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a US-style check-the-box or pass-through election. A Yuhan Hoesa is categorically classified as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed at entity level on worldwide income. The group consolidation tax regime is available only as a filing measure for qualifying wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries and is not an entity classification election. Anti-hybrid and structural mismatch rules under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs apply as mandatory law and cannot be elected away.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0: there is no general turnover threshold before VAT registration becomes mandatory in Korea. Registration is compulsory upon commencing taxable supplies. The simplified taxable person concession is limited to individual entrepreneurs with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million and is not available to a Yuhan Hoesa corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a centralized electronic tax invoice mandate through the HomeTax e-tax invoice service. Business suppliers must issue tax invoices by the statutory deadline; those invoices must be transmitted electronically to the NTS for B2B supplies, and NTS cross-matches invoice data with VAT returns and customs records. Cash receipts are required for consumer cash transactions. Korea does not use a Latin American-style real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping model; there is no transaction-level pre-approval API. Instead, the NTS uses consolidated e-tax invoice submission, pre-refund risk scoring, and automated post-event audits, supported by the KCS UNI-PASS customs data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT is the mandatory statutory treatment for exports of goods under the Value-Added Tax Act. For subscription-box merchandising, the Korean entity must prove: (1) the goods physically left Korea under an accepted export declaration to the Korea Customs Service; (2) the recipient is a non-resident customer and title/risk passed outside Korea; (3) the export is recorded in the Korean entity's books as an export sale; (4) the proceeds are paid in foreign currency and repatriated to a Korean foreign exchange bank; and (5) the complete export evidence pack is retained. Digitally supplied services performed in Korea but supplied to a non-resident and actually used overseas may also qualify for zero-rating if paid in foreign currency; however, the physical goods in a subscription box must satisfy the physical export and customs documentation route.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration clearance certificate (UNI-PASS Export Declaration clearance)
Bill of Lading (sea) or Air Waybill (air) showing the Korean exporter as shipper and a foreign consignee/destination outside Korea
Commercial invoice stating FOB/export value of the subscription box
Packing list itemizing the contents, quantities, and HS codes of the subscription box
Foreign exchange settlement confirmation or Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match e-tax invoices, export declarations, and foreign exchange bank settlement records. An exporter that cannot substantiate the zero-rated export within the statutory deadline may have the supply recharacterized as domestic: 10% VAT is assessed, input VAT refunds are recovered by correction order, interest is charged from the date of refund, and additional tax is imposed under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 270-day foreign exchange settlement deadline can also invalidate the zero-rating evidence. False tax invoices, fraudulent refund claims, or deliberate misstatement are referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with criminal penalties, retrospective clawback of refunds, and potential suspension or revocation of future export zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with foreign exchange policy authority coordinated with the Ministry of Strategy and Finance, and transaction-level administration delegated by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act to licensed domestic foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a market-friendly, largely liberalized foreign exchange regime rather than a strict exchange-control system. The Korean won is fully convertible for current transactions, including trade settlements, travel, and dividend remittances, provided the underlying documentation and bank declarations are complete under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. Capital and financial account transactions are conditionally liberalized: inbound foreign direct investment into a Yuhan Hoesa must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act or the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and each inward remittance must be declared to the receiving foreign exchange bank for reporting to the Bank of Korea. There is no mandatory surrender requirement, and foreign investors may retain USD, KRW, or other currencies in domestic foreign-exchange accounts. The principal economic friction is documentary, not regulatory: profit remittances require audited earnings evidence, certificate of tax withholding, compensation-related tax receipts, and confirmation that no restrictions on outward remittance apply. Because Korea uses a free-floating regime with FX risk borne by market participants, the treasury must use covered hedging instruments only for genuine underlying exposures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Korea's Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters must collect foreign currency proceeds within six months from the date of export declaration unless an extension is approved by the designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Strategy and Finance. There is no mandatory conversion into KRW; the current statutory surrender ratio is 0% and proceeds may be held, used for foreign-currency payments, converted voluntarily, or deposited into a registered foreign-exchange account. Exporters must submit a receipt report through the receiving bank to the Bank of Korea. Late receipt requires a written explanation and can trigger administrative penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: KRW Operating/Current Account and Foreign Currency Deposit Account
Capital Escrow Account and Trade Settlement Account
KRW Recurring Collections Account and FX Hedging Account
Operational/Clearing Account for Payment Gateway Settlements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall viability for treasury purposes: low. South Korea does not grant cross-border e-money institution (EMI) licenses to foreign fintechs under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act; a foreign EMI cannot hold deposits, provide local IBANs, or clear Korean won settlement for a Yuhan Hoesa unless it establishes a licensed local subsidiary or partners with a licensed bank as its settlement agent. Offshore digital platforms such as Stripe and Authorize.Net can support card collection as acquirers or payment processors, but final net settlement must be into a domestic Tier-1 bank account. Using an offshore EMI as the treasury account would create illegal deposit-taking, unreported foreign-exchange flows, and AML opacity. The correct treasury posture is to treat Stripe and Authorize.Net as payment collection rails only, with automatic daily or T+1 sweep to the Korean operating account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, physical attendance is mandatory for at least one authorized representative. A non-resident sole member or statutory director of a Yuhan Hoesa must attend one in-person onboarding interview at the Korean branch, or, at selected global banks, at an overseas branch with a video interview with the Korean KYC officer. Consular proxy opening is not generally accepted as a substitute because real-name verification rules under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act require the bank to confirm the signer's identity. If the entity has no domestic signatory, the foreign board can issue a notarized power of attorney to a Korean tax or legal representative, but the foreign beneficial owner must still complete a video interview and submit apostilled identity documents. The bank will also require a corporate seal certificate, which may require physical production of the seal and constitutional documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border mismatch between the beneficial owner's tax residency, the foreign subscriber base, and the stated card-not-present subscription business, creating suspicion of unverified third-party payment flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated transaction flow evidence including the registered business license, board-approved share register showing final beneficial owners, bank statements with incoming Stripe and Authorize.Net settlement files, platform sales records showing distinct goods and recurring order logic, source-of-funds declarations for any capital injection, and certified English/Korean apostilled passports and residence proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring physical export and inventory import movements for subscription boxes without supporting trade documentation, which may resemble trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs declaration records, HS-code mapping for each SKU, supplier invoices and contracts, warehouse inventory count confirmations, freight forwarder bills of lading or airway bills, and a treasury policy that third-party supply payments are made only to named supplier bank accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High frequency of refunds, chargebacks, or variable recurring amounts triggering merchant-acquirer AML and terrorist financing monitoring under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cancellation and refund policy documentation, order-management audit logs, chargeback reason codes, sales tax and VAT remittance schedules, and a documented refund matching report tied to the original payment token, together with a monthly recurring revenue statement for the compliance committee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital remittance from a non-resident personal account or a non-bank money service business rather than from the beneficial owner's audited corporate account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign direct investment registration certificate or bank-issued capital inflow report, bank confirmation of source of funds such as salary or audited profits, tax clearance certificate from the originator jurisdiction, and legal entity ownership documentation showing the remitting shareholder exactly matches the registered member.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound paid-in capital must use a SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's institutional account to the Yuhan Hoesa's capital escrow account at the designated Korean bank. The remittance instruction must quote the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act filing reference and state the Bank of Korea FX transaction purpose code corresponding to inward direct investment equity contribution. The receiving bank will verify the code against the Foreign Investment Promotion Act report, perform capital verification, issue the foreign-investment registration certificate, and only then release funds to the operating account. Cash deposits, crypto conversions, and interposed fintech wallets are not acceptable. After verification, the funds may be used for subscription-box inventory procurement, warehousing, and merchant service fees. Inbound remittances above the applicable threshold require advance declaration; funds originating from tax havens or sanctioned jurisdictions will be escalated.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments under roughly USD 500,000 equivalent, with the underlying contract number and Bank of Korea purpose code in the remittance text. For larger inventory orders, protect the entity with an irrevocable confirmed commercial letter of credit issued by the Korean bank in favor of the foreign supplier, negotiated under UCP600. For recurring low-value subscription-box component imports, a documentary collection on a monthly basis backed by a clean freight-forwarder package is acceptable. All outbound wires must carry the relevant contract or purchase order number and BOK FX purpose code; payments to related parties must be supported by transfer pricing documentation. Overseas customer card collections may be channelled through Stripe or Authorize.Net and settled in KRW by a licensed acquiring bank, but never moved through offshore EMI accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, limited to documented current trade exposures with the underlying invoice, contract, or order schedule maintained by the treasury.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) traded only with an authorized Korean bank under confirmed underlying KRW receivables or payables, and never for speculative purposes.

Cross-currency swaps for medium-term foreign-currency debt or capital exposure, subject to formal bank credit approval and evidence that the instruments are matched to an underlying asset or liability.

Plain-vanilla FX options on a covered basis where the option premium and notional align strictly with the treasury's forecast subscription revenue or inventory imports; uncovered option writing and speculative strategies are not permissible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS-HomeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year immediately following a calendar taxable year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 3 months after the fiscal year end; a return-preparation extension of up to 1 month may be available through a licensed tax accountant, but the tax payment remains due by the original deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and underreporting: NTS additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax (40% for false or fraudulent omission); late payment: daily arrears charge of 0.022% on the overdue amount; after 30 days, NTS may issue demand and seize assets; repeated deliberate non-filing can lead to administrative cancellation of the business registration and criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Portion (Local Income Tax on Corporate Income)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Metropolitan City, Province, Si, Gun or Gu Local Tax Authority via WeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 30 of the year immediately following a calendar taxable year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, within 4 months after the fiscal year end, i.e., 1 month after the corporate income tax filing deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and non-payment: local tax additional charge of 20% of the unpaid local income tax (40% for false returns), daily arrears charge of 0.022%, and compulsory collection by the local government; continued non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary and Final Returns (Four Electronic VAT Filings per Year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary VAT returns by April 25 for January-March and by October 25 for July-September; final VAT returns by July 25 for January-June and by January 25 for July-December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT Act penalties: 20% additional tax on omitted VAT payable (40% for fraudulent omission), additional tax for excessive input tax refunds, and a penalty of 0.5% of the supply value for failure to issue an electronic tax invoice; daily arrears interest accrues on late payment; gross and continuous non-filing can result in administrative cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements (if asset threshold or designation is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission, Financial Supervisory Service DART (where applicable), and National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year company, the independent auditor must complete the audit and the audited financial statements must be available for attachment to the corporate income tax return by March 31; if subject to FSS DART filing, the audit report is filed electronically by March 31 or within 90 days after fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain a mandatory external audit is a violation of the Act on External Audit of Corporations; the company and responsible directors may be fined up to KRW 50 million, the NTS may reject unaudited financial statements and impose unfavorable adjustments, and directors may be jointly and severally liable for damages to members and creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry and Foreign Investment Change Registration Protocol (Event-based Annual Monitoring)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Court Commercial Registration Office; designated Foreign Exchange Bank and KOTRA for non-resident ownership changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days from the date of any registry-required change (e.g., registered office relocation, director or representative officer change, or membership interest transfer); non-resident ownership changes must be reported to the designated Foreign Exchange Bank/KOTRA within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late commercial registry filing: administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Act; an unregistered membership transfer is ineffective against third parties; late foreign investment change reporting may attract a Foreign Exchange Transactions Act penalty of up to KRW 20 million and adverse exchange-control treatment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Registers Verification and Refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing authority; registers are maintained at the registered office and produced on demand to the District Court, NTS, FSC, or external auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance requirement; full annual verification should be completed on or before March 31 of each year, aligned with the corporate income tax and local income tax filing season.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete, inaccurate, or missing statutory registers violate the Commercial Act and may subject the company to administrative fines of up to KRW 5 million, personal liability of directors for damages caused to members or creditors, and criminal liability for forged or knowingly false register entries.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Corporations, an annual independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory if the Yuhan Hoesa meets any of the following as of fiscal year end: (1) balance-sheet trigger: total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.9 million at KRW 1,350/USD); (2) public-market trigger: securities are listed, traded, or publicly offered; (3) designation trigger: the Financial Services Commission, after Securities and Futures Commission deliberation, designates the company by enforcement decree, which may consider total assets, total revenue, and headcount; this can capture a non-listed company with revenue of KRW 50 billion or more or 300 or more full-time employees where public interest requires audit; (4) supervised financial company or financial holding company subsidiary, regardless of size; or (5) parent or affiliate in a business group required to undergo a consolidated external audit. There is no standalone turnover or headcount audit mandate for a private Yuhan Hoesa; revenue and headcount operate as designation factors only. The audit must be performed by a certified public accountant registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements are prepared under K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for listed or publicly accountable entities, or if the company elects K-IFRS; a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (KA-GAAP) under the Act on External Audit of Corporations and External Audit Standards; a small or medium-sized unlisted company within qualifying statutory limits may apply Korean SME Accounting Standards (SME K-GAAP). All statutory financial statements must be maintained in Korean language and Korean currency (KRW), with appropriate foreign currency translation in accordance with the applicable accounting standard.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a current register of members showing each member's name, membership interest, date of acquisition, and all transfers. Every transfer of a membership interest must be recorded promptly in the register of members, and an amendment to the Commercial Registry must be filed with the District Court Registration Office within 14 days of the change in order for the transfer to be effective against third parties. For non-resident ownership, the foreign investor must report any transfer of the membership interest to the designated Foreign Exchange Bank and to KOTRA within 30 days under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. There is no separate annual nationwide UBO renewal form for a private, non-listed LLC; the annual confirmation is satisfied by updating the register of members, completing the Commercial Registry amendment where applicable, disclosing ultimate beneficial ownership in the corporate income tax return attachments, and retaining contemporaneous ownership and transfer evidence at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (including membership interests and pledges)
Register of Charges / Mortgages (encumbrances over assets and pledged membership interests)
Minute Book of Members' General Meetings and Directors' Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,500 per year for a Korean registered office address and local corporate agent service, inclusive of NTS/WeTax correspondence handling and mail forwarding
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - 30,000 for a separately audited Korean LLC; not applicable if the entity remains below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold and is not otherwise designated by the Financial Services Commission

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% (up to KRW 200 million) / 19% (KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion) / 21% (KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion) / 24% (above KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax, producing a maximum combined headline burden of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No generic patent box, but substantive incentives exist: (i) reduced statutory corporate income tax rates for qualifying small and medium enterprises; (ii) up to 50% tax credits for research and development expenses under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act; (iii) job-creation and facility-investment tax credits; and (iv) foreign investment zone and free economic zone incentives that may exempt corporate income tax for 3 to 5 tax years and reduce the following 2 years by 50%, subject to minimum investment and locally substantive employment and business requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National Tax Service Form 12 - Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Return for a foreign corporation branch, together with Schedule 12-1 (taxable income), Schedule 12-2 (local income tax), and the International Transaction Report, filed electronically through the HomeTax portal at www.hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional prepayment declarations after the first, second and third quarters; the annual return is a final settlement of the quarterly prepayment amounts.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; a calendar-year company must file by 31 March. A 15-day extension applies when the return is prepared and certified by a Korean tax accountant or by an external auditor; the National Tax Service may exercise discretion to grant an additional extension for foreign-controlled corporate groups that require cross-border accounting closing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Corporate registration number and taxpayer identity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean business entity legal name, corporate business registration number, head office address, domestic place of business address and representative director details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the unique Korean business registration number issued to Yuhan Hoesa or its Korean permanent establishment (PE). Do not use the foreign parent company tax identification number as the primary Korean identity. If no individual with a Korean address is available as the responsible officer, electronically appoint a tax representative on HomeTax and attach the power of attorney before the return is submitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - Korean-source taxable base before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Korean-source income under Article 93 of the Corporate Tax Act, less exempt income and deductible expenses actually attributable to the Korean business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all recurring subscription box payments collected, fulfilled or processed through a Korean address or Korean payment gateway, because those receipts are Korean-source business income for ISIC_4791_08. If the foreign head office holds customer contracts or payment rights, attribute the entire arm's length profit to the Korean PE and adjust all intercompany markups under the controlled transaction standard; do not treat a foreign invoice as creating a deductible cost unless the service or product is genuinely rendered to the Korean entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - Deduction of losses brought forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of Korean eligible net operating losses (NOL) brought forward from prior fiscal years to offset the current taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korean losses using the standard method may be carried forward for 15 years, but only when the Korean entity has filed complete tax returns and maintained independent Korean books. A foreign shareholder cannot use Korean NOL because the losses belong to the Korean taxpayer; if the Yuhan Hoesa is a branch, losses of the head office cannot be deducted in Korea and must be recomputed exclusively from Korean activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 10 - National corporate income tax at progressive rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax computed by applying the statutory progressive brackets to the taxable base before foreign tax credit and special credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9%, 19%, 21% and 24% statutory brackets to Korean taxable income only. The local income tax surcharge is then calculated at 10% of the national corporate tax. A non-resident corporation may not take a foreign tax credit on this line for taxes paid to the foreign jurisdiction unless a relevant Korean tax treaty expressly provides for a credit mechanism applicable to a Korean PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 14 - Quarterly prepayments and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total quarterly provisional corporate tax payments, domestic withholding credits, and foreign tax credits valid for taxes embedded in the Korean taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach NTS payment receipts for each quarterly prepayment. When a Korean payer has withheld non-resident tax under Article 98 of the Corporate Tax Act, the credit is allowed only if the withholding certificate, the Form 23 application, the Tax Residency Certificate and the beneficial ownership statement are all consecutively documented. A foreign parent must not claim a Korean credit for withholding paid by a different legal entity or by a foreign branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 19 / Box 20 - Total tax due and local income tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final national corporate tax due plus the 10% local income tax surcharge, reduced by credits and prepayments, showing the net amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Yuhan Hoesa is a Korean taxable entity, the final amount must be paid from the Korean corporate bank account. If the entity is a non-resident with only a Korean PE, the return finalizes the PE tax; do not report a final dividend withholding amount on this line because branch profits may be subject to a separate branch-level remittance tax only when actually repatriated to certain treaty jurisdictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file triggers a 20% failure-to-file additional tax on the unpaid tax; a filed return that understates tax triggers a 10% unfaithful-return surcharge, increased to 40% where the understatement is fraudulent. Late payment is subject to daily arrears surcharges at the statutory rate, approximately 0.022% per day for the first three months and 0.030% thereafter. Criminal tax evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to twice the evaded tax, or imprisonment up to 10 years and an enhanced fine where the evaded tax exceeds KRW 500 million. Omission of the mandatory International Transaction Report also attracts a separate surcharge of 5% of the unreported transaction amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% aggregate outbound dividend withholding on dividends paid by Yuhan Hoesa to non-resident shareholders: 20% national dividend withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge (10% of the 20% national withholding), under Article 98(1) of the Corporate Tax Act and the Local Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke bilateral Double Tax Treaty relief, the following administrative process is mandatory: (1) obtain an apostilled Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign shareholder competent authority, issued for the same calendar year as the dividend distribution; (2) file a written Application for Reduction or Exemption of Non-Resident Withholding Tax (Form 23) with the Korean payer prior to the payment date; (3) attach a shareholder ownership chart, control certificate and beneficial ownership declaration evidencing that the ultimate recipient is the real owner and not a conduit, with employees, premises, management and business activity in its state of residence; (4) the Korean payer may then withhold at the treaty rate; if the full statutory amount has been withheld, the non-resident owner may claim a refund from the National Tax Service within 5 years of payment. The reduction or exemption is denied if the recipient cannot prove beneficial ownership or if the arrangement has no economic substance and is intended solely to obtain treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic statutory withholding rate on outbound royalties and interest to non-resident corporations is also 22%, being 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge. Under Korea DTA treaties, treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10%-15% and royalties to 10%-15%, frequently 10% for industrial, commercial or scientific equipment royalties and 15% for most copyright and software royalties. The same Form 23, Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership substantiation process is required to apply any treaty rate and is an absolute precondition for relief from over-withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is required when the aggregate volume of foreign related-party transactions in sales, purchases, loans, royalties, service fees and security subscription transactions equals or exceeds KRW 5 billion in a fiscal year. The International Transaction Report must also be attached to the Korean corporate tax return at that threshold. A Country-by-Country report is separately required when the multinational group's consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute, but the same doctrine is mandatorily applied through Article 15 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, Article 14 of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, and treaty limitation-on-benefits jurisprudence. The National Tax Service will disregard a shell entity, reallocate Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) to Yuhan Hoesa's Korean office, and impute a Korean permanent establishment when subscription-box contract negotiation, customer support, inventory management, order fulfillment, payment collection and strategic decision-making are performed in Korea. A foreign nominee that merely signs paper contracts and records invoices in a zero-tax jurisdiction will not receive treaty protection.
